rules.title: KYC Policy Framework
rules.description: Banks should frame their KYC policies incorporating four key elements: Customer Acceptance Policy, Customer Identification Procedure, Monitoring of Transactions, and Risk Management.
rules.source_clause: Banks should frame their KYC policies incorporating the following four key elements: (a) Customer Acceptance Policy; (b) Customer Identification Procedure; (c) Monitoring of Transactions; and (d) Risk Management.

rules.title: Customer Acceptance Policy
rules.description: Every bank should develop a clear Customer Acceptance Policy laying down explicit criteria for acceptance of customers, including no account in anonymous or fictitious/benami name(s), parameters of risk perception, documentation requirements, and no account opening or existing account closure where the bank is unable to apply appropriate customer due diligence measures.
rules.source_clause: 2.3 Customer Acceptance Policy (CAP) (a) Every bank should develop a clear Customer Acceptance Policy laying down explicit criteria for acceptance of customers.

rules.title: Risk Categorization
rules.description: Banks should categorize customers into low, medium, and high risk based on parameters such as nature of business activity, location of customer and his clients, mode of payments, volume of turnover, social and financial status, etc.
rules.source_clause: (ii)  Parameters of risk perception are clearly defined in terms of the nature of business activity, location of customer and his clients, mode of payments, volume of turnover, social and financial status etc. to enable categorisation of customers into low, medium and high risk

rules.title: Customer Identification Procedure
rules.description: Banks should clearly spell out the Customer Identification Procedure to be carried out at different stages, including while establishing a banking relationship, carrying out a financial transaction, or when the bank has a doubt about the authenticity/veracity or the adequacy of the previously obtained customer identification data.
rules.source_clause: The policy approved by the Board of banks should clearly spell out the Customer Identification Procedure to be carried out at different stages i.e. while establishing a banking relationship, carrying out a financial transaction or when the bank has a doubt about the authenticity/veracity or the adequacy of the previously obtained customer identification data.

rules.title: Mandatory and Optional Information
rules.description: Banks should obtain only the 'mandatory' information required for KYC purpose at the time of opening the account/during periodic updation. Other 'optional' customer details/additional information, if required, may be obtained separately after the account is opened only with the explicit consent of the customer.
rules.source_clause: (ii) Banks should ensure that any remittance of funds by way of demand draft, mail/telegraphic transfer or any other mode and issue of travellers’ cheques for value of Rupees fifty thousand and above is effected by debit to the customer’s account or against cheques and not against cash payment.

rules.title: Remittance of Funds
rules.description: Banks should ensure that any remittance of funds by way of demand draft, mail/telegraphic transfer or any other mode and issue of travellers' cheques for value of Rupees fifty thousand and above is effected by debit to the customer's account or against cheques and not against cash payment.
rules.source_clause: (ii) Banks should ensure that any remittance of funds by way of demand draft, mail/telegraphic transfer or any other mode and issue of travellers' cheques for value of Rupees fifty thousand and above is effected by debit to the customer's account or against cheques and not against cash payment.

rules.title: Verify Identity of Customers
rules.description: Banks must verify the identity of customers through proper and relevant documents, and understand the ownership and control structure of the customer.
rules.source_clause: (ii) verify that any person purporting to act on behalf of the legal person/entity is so authorised and identify and verify the identity of that person; (iii) understand the ownership and control structure of the customer and determine who are the natural persons who ultimately control the legal person.

rules.title: KYC Requirements for Low-Risk Customers
rules.description: Full KYC exercise is required to be done at least every ten years for low-risk individuals and entities.
rules.source_clause: Full KYC exercise will be required to be done at least every ten years for low risk and at least every eight years for medium risk individuals and entities.

rules.title: KYC Requirements for High-Risk Customers
rules.description: Full KYC exercise is required to be done at least every two years for high-risk individuals and entities.
rules.source_clause: Full KYC exercise will be required to be done at least every two years for high risk individuals and entities.

rules.title: Positive Confirmation for Low-Risk Customers
rules.description: Positive confirmation is required to be completed at least every three years for low-risk individuals and entities.
rules.source_clause: Positive confirmation (obtaining KYC related updates through e-mail / letter / telephonic conversation / forms / interviews / visits, etc.) will be required to be completed at least every two years for medium risk and at least every three years for low risk individuals and entities.

rules.title: Unique Customer Identification Code (UCIC)
rules.description: Banks are advised to allot UCIC to all their customers while entering into any new relationships.
rules.source_clause: Banks are, therefore, advised to allot UCIC to all their customers while entering into any new relationships for individual customers to begin with.

rules.title: Verification of Trust/Nominee or Fiduciary Accounts
rules.description: Banks should determine whether the customer is acting on behalf of another person as trustee/nominee or any other intermediary and verify the identity of the intermediaries and the persons on whose behalf they are acting.
rules.source_clause: Banks should determine whether the customer is acting on behalf of another person as trustee/nominee or any other intermediary. If so, banks should insist on receipt of satisfactory evidence of the identity of the intermediaries and of the persons on whose behalf they are acting, as also obtain details of the nature of the trust or other arrangements in place.

rules.title: Verification of Accounts of Companies and Firms
rules.description: Banks need to examine the control structure of the entity, determine the source of funds and identify the natural persons who have a controlling interest and who comprise the management.
rules.source_clause: Banks need to be vigilant against business entities being used by individuals as a ‘front’ for maintaining accounts with banks. Banks should examine the control structure of the entity, determine the source of funds and identify the natural persons who have a controlling interest and who comprise the management.

rules.title: Verification of Client Accounts Opened by Professional Intermediaries
rules.description: When the bank has knowledge or reason to believe that the client account opened by a professional intermediary is on behalf of a single client, that client must be identified.
rules.source_clause: When the bank has knowledge or reason to believe that the client account opened by a professional intermediary is on behalf of a single client, that client must be identified.

rules.title: KYC Requirements for Intermediaries
rules.description: Banks should ensure that intermediaries are regulated, supervised, and have adequate systems in place to comply with KYC requirements.
rules.source_clause: intermediary is regulated and supervised and has adequate systems in place to comply with the KYC requirements.

rules.title: No Accounts for Intermediaries with Confidentiality Obligations
rules.description: Banks should not allow professional intermediaries with confidentiality obligations to open or hold accounts if they cannot disclose the true identity of the account owner.
rules.source_clause: Banks should not allow opening and / or holding of an account on behalf of a client/s by professional intermediaries, like lawyers and chartered accountants, etc., who are unable to disclose the true identity of the owner of the account / funds due to professional obligation of customer confidentiality.

rules.title: Verification of Beneficial Owners
rules.description: Banks should identify and verify the beneficial owners of clients, including natural persons exercising control through ownership interests or other means.
rules.source_clause: A. Where the client is a person other than an individual or trust, the banking company and financial institution, as the case may be, shall identify the beneficial owners of the client and take reasonable measures to verify the identity of such persons, through the following information :

rules.title: Accounts of Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs)
rules.description: Banks should gather sufficient information on PEPs, verify their identity, and seek information about the sources of funds before accepting them as customers.
rules.source_clause: Banks should gather sufficient information on any person/customer of this category intending to establish a relationship and check all the information available on the person in the public domain.

rules.title: Verify Walk-in Customer Identity
rules.description: In case of transactions carried out by a non-account based customer, that is a walk-in customer, where the amount of transaction is equal to or exceeds Rupees fifty thousand, whether conducted as a single transaction or several transactions that appear to be connected, the customer’s identity and address should be verified.
rules.source_clause: In case of transactions carried out by a non-account based customer, that is a walk-in customer, where the amount of transaction is equal to or exceeds Rupees fifty thousand, whether conducted as a single transaction or several transactions that appear to be connected, the customer’s identity and address should be verified.

rules.title: FPI KYC Verification
rules.description: FPIs who have been duly registered in accordance with SEBI guidelines and have undergone the required KYC due diligence/verification prescribed by SEBI through a Custodian / Intermediary regulated by SEBI may approach Authorised Dealer (AD) Category-I StCBs for opening a bank account for the purpose of investment under Portfolio Investment Scheme (PIS) for which KYC documents prescribed by RBI would be required.
rules.source_clause: FPIs who have been duly registered in accordance with SEBI guidelines and have undergone the required KYC due diligence/verification prescribed by SEBI through a Custodian / Intermediary regulated by SEBI may approach Authorised Dealer (AD) Category-I StCBs for opening a bank account for the purpose of investment under Portfolio Investment Scheme (PIS) for which KYC documents prescribed by RBI (Annex VI-B) would be required.

rules.title: Money Mule Prevention
rules.description: Banks are advised to strictly adhere to the guidelines on KYC/AML/CFT issued from time to time and to those relating to periodical updation of customer identification data after the account is opened and also to monitoring of transactions in order to protect themselves and their customers from misuse by such fraudsters.
rules.source_clause: Banks are, therefore, advised to strictly adhere to the guidelines on KYC/AML/CFT issued from time to time and to those relating to periodical updation of customer identification data after the account is opened and also to monitoring of transactions in order to protect themselves and their customers from misuse by such fraudsters.

rules.title: Ongoing Monitoring of Transactions
rules.description: Ongoing monitoring is an essential element of effective KYC procedures. Banks can effectively control and reduce their risk only if they have an understanding of the normal and reasonable activity of the customer so that they have the means of identifying transactions that fall outside the regular pattern of activity.
rules.source_clause: Ongoing monitoring is an essential element of effective KYC procedures. Banks can effectively control and reduce their risk only if they have an understanding of the normal and reasonable activity of the customer so that they have the means of identifying transactions that fall outside the regular pattern of activity.

rules.title: Risk Categorization of Accounts
rules.description: Every bank should set key indicators for such accounts, taking note of the background of the customer, such as the country of origin, sources of funds, the type of transactions involved and other risk factors. Banks should put in place a system of periodical review of risk categorization of accounts and the need for applying enhanced due diligence measures.
rules.source_clause: Every bank should set key indicators for such accounts, taking note of the background of the customer, such as the country of origin, sources of funds, the type of transactions involved and other risk factors. Banks should put in place a system of periodical review of risk categorization of accounts and the need for applying enhanced due diligence measures.

rules.title: Closure of Accounts
rules.description: Banks should ensure that all the existing accounts are subjected to minimum KYC standards which would establish the identity of the natural / legal person and those of the ‘beneficial owners.’ Where the bank is unable to apply appropriate KYC measures due to non-furnishing of information and /or non-cooperation by the customer, the bank should consider closing the account or terminating the banking/business relationship after issuing due notice to the customer explaining the reasons for taking such a decision.
rules.source_clause: Banks should ensure that all the existing accounts are subjected to minimum KYC standards which would establish the identity of the natural / legal person and those of the ‘beneficial owners.’ Where the bank is unable to apply appropriate KYC measures due to non-furnishing of information and /or non-cooperation by the customer, the bank should consider closing the account or terminating the banking/business relationship after issuing due notice to the customer explaining the reasons for taking such a decision.

rules.title: Risk Management
rules.description: The Board of Directors of the bank should ensure that an effective KYC programme is put in place by establishing appropriate procedures and ensuring their effective implementation. It should cover proper management oversight, systems and controls, segregation of duties, training and other related matters.
rules.source_clause: (a) The Board of Directors of the bank should ensure that an effective KYC programme is put in place by establishing appropriate procedures and ensuring their effective implementation. It should cover proper management oversight, systems and controls, segregation of duties, training and other related matters.

rules.title: KYC/AML/CFT Guidelines for Cardholders
rules.description: Banks are required to ensure full compliance with all KYC/AML/CFT guidelines issued from time to time, in respect of add-on/supplementary cardholders also.
rules.source_clause: Banks are required to ensure full compliance with all KYC/AML/CFT guidelines issued from time to time, in respect of add-on/ supplementary cardholders also.

rules.title: Utilization of 'At Par' Cheque Facility
rules.description: Banks are advised to utilize the 'at par' cheque facility only for their own use, their account holders who are KYC compliant, and 'walk-in customers' against cash for less than Rupees fifty thousand per individual.
rules.source_clause: banks are advised to utilize the ‘at par’ cheque facility only for: i) their own use; ii) their account holders who are KYC compliant provided that all transactions of Rupees fifty thousand or more should be strictly by debit to the customer’s account; iii) 'walk-in customers' against cash for less than Rupees fifty thousand per individual.

rules.title: Crossing 'At Par' Cheques
rules.description: Banks should ensure that all 'at par' cheques issued by them are crossed 'account payee' irrespective of the amount involved.
rules.source_clause: Banks should also ensure that all ‘at par’ cheques issued by them are crossed ‘account payee’ irrespective of the amount involved.

rules.title: Monitoring of Accounts with Terrorist Links
rules.description: Banks are advised to develop a suitable mechanism through an appropriate policy framework for enhanced monitoring of accounts suspected of having terrorist links and swift identification of transactions.
rules.source_clause: Banks are, therefore, advised to develop suitable mechanism through appropriate policy framework for enhanced monitoring of accounts suspected of having terrorist links and swift identification of the transactions and making suitable reports to the Financial Intelligence Unit – India (FIU-IND) on priority.

rules.title: Updating of UNSCR Lists
rules.description: Banks should ensure to update the consolidated list of individuals and entities as circulated by the Reserve Bank.
rules.source_clause: Banks should ensure to update the consolidated list of individuals and entities as circulated by the Reserve Bank.

rules.title: Verification of Customer Names against UNSCR Lists
rules.description: Before opening any new account, banks should ensure that the name/s of the proposed customer does not appear in either list.
rules.source_clause: before opening any new account, it should be ensured that the name/s of the proposed customer does not appear in either list.

rules.title: Freezing of Financial Assets
rules.description: On receipt of the particulars, IS-I Division of MHA would cause a verification to be conducted by the State Police and/or the Central Agencies so as to ensure that the individuals/entities identified by the banks are the ones listed as designated individuals/entities.
rules.source_clause: (i)  Maintain updated designated lists in electronic form and run a check on the given parameters on a regular basis to verify whether individuals or entities listed   in    the    Schedule   to    the   Order   (referred   to   as designated individuals/entities) are holding any funds, financial assets or economic resources or related services held in the form of bank accounts with them.

rules.title: Freezing Assets of Designated Individuals/Entities
rules.description: In case the results of verification indicate that properties are owned by or held for the benefit of designated individuals/entities, an order to freeze these assets under Section 51-A of the UAPA would be issued within 24 hours of such verification.
rules.source_clause: (ii) In case, the results of the verification indicate that the properties are owned by or held for the benefit of the designated individuals/entities, an order to freeze these assets under Section 51-A of the UAPA would be issued within 24 hours of such verification and conveyed electronically to the bank branch concerned under intimation to the Reserve Bank and FIU-IND.

rules.title: No Prior Notice for Freezing Orders
rules.description: The Order shall take place without prior notice to the designated individuals/entities.
rules.source_clause: (iii) The Order shall take place without prior notice to the designated individuals/entities.

rules.title: Implementation of UNSCR 1373 Requests
rules.description: The Ministry of External Affairs shall examine requests made by foreign countries and forward them electronically to the UAPA nodal officer for IS-I Division for freezing of funds or other assets.
rules.source_clause: (ii) The Ministry of External Affairs shall examine the requests made by the foreign countries and forward it electronically, with their comments, to the UAPA nodal officer for IS-I Division for freezing of funds or other assets, to give effect to the requests of foreign countries under UNSCR 1373.

rules.title: Communication of Freezing Orders
rules.description: All Orders under Section 51A of Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 relating to funds, financial assets or economic resources or related services, would be communicated to all banks through the Reserve Bank.
rules.source_clause: All Orders under Section 51A of Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967 relating to funds, financial assets or economic resources or related services, would be communicated to all banks through the Reserve Bank.

rules.title: Unfreezing of Inadvertently Frozen Funds
rules.description: Any individual or entity, if it has evidence to prove that the freezing of funds, financial assets or economic resources or related services, owned /held by them has been inadvertently frozen, they shall move an application giving the requisite evidence, in writing, to the bank concerned.
rules.source_clause: (f) Procedure for unfreezing of funds, financial assets or economic resources or related services of individuals/entities inadvertently affected by the freezing mechanism upon verification that the person or entity is not a designated persons

rules.title: FATF Recommendations
rules.description: Banks are required to take into account risks arising from the deficiencies in AML/CFT regime of the jurisdictions included in the FATF Statement.
rules.source_clause: (a) Banks are required to take into account risks arising from the deficiencies in AML/CFT regime of the jurisdictions included in the FATF Statement.

rules.title: Correspondent Banking Relationships
rules.description: Banks should gather sufficient information to understand fully the nature of the business of the correspondent/respondent bank.
rules.source_clause: (a) Correspondent banking is the provision of banking services by one bank (the “correspondent bank”) to another bank (the “respondent bank”). These services may include cash/funds management, international wire transfers, drawing arrangements for demand drafts and mail transfers, payable-through-accounts, cheques clearing etc. Banks should gather sufficient information to understand fully the nature of the business of the correspondent/respondent bank.

rules.title: Shell Banks
rules.description: Banks should refuse to enter into a correspondent relationship with a ‘shell bank’ (i.e. a bank which is incorporated in a country where it has no physical presence and is unaffiliated to any regulated financial group).
rules.source_clause: Banks should refuse to enter into a correspondent relationship with a ‘shell bank’ (i.e. a bank which is incorporated in a country where it has no physical presence and is unaffiliated to any regulated financial group).

rules.title: Wire Transfer Information
rules.description: Banks use wire transfers as an expeditious method for transferring funds between bank accounts and should ensure that basic information on the originator of wire transfers is immediately available to appropriate law enforcement.
rules.source_clause: (b) Wire transfer is an instantaneous and most preferred route for transfer of funds across the globe and hence, there is a need for preventing terrorists and other criminals from having unfettered access to wire transfers for moving their funds and for detecting any misuse when it occurs.

rules.title: Cross-border wire transfers require originator information
rules.description: All cross-border wire transfers must be accompanied by accurate and meaningful originator information, including name and address of the originator and account number or unique reference number.
rules.source_clause: All cross-border wire transfers must be accompanied by accurate and meaningful originator information.

rules.title: Domestic wire transfers over Rs. 50,000 require originator information
rules.description: Information accompanying all domestic wire transfers of Rupees fifty thousand and above must include complete originator information.
rules.source_clause: Information accompanying all domestic wire transfers of Rupees fifty thousand and above must include complete originator information i.e. name, address and account number etc.,

rules.title: Structuring transactions to avoid reporting
rules.description: If a bank has reason to believe that a customer is intentionally structuring wire transfer to below Rupees fifty thousand to several beneficiaries in order to avoid reporting or monitoring, the bank must insist on complete customer identification.
rules.source_clause: If a bank has reason to believe that a customer is intentionally structuring wire transfer to below Rupees fifty thousand to several beneficiaries in order to avoid reporting or monitoring, the bank must insist on complete customer identification before effecting the transfer.

rules.title: Ordering bank responsibilities
rules.description: The ordering bank must ensure that qualifying wire transfers contain complete originator information and verify and preserve the information at least for a period of ten years.
rules.source_clause: The ordering bank must ensure that qualifying wire transfers contain complete originator information. The bank must also verify and preserve the information at least for a period of ten years.

rules.title: Intermediary bank responsibilities
rules.description: For both cross-border and domestic wire transfers, a bank processing an intermediary element of a chain of wire transfers must ensure that all originator information accompanying a wire transfer is retained with the transfer.
rules.source_clause: For both cross-border and domestic wire transfers, a bank processing an intermediary element of a chain of wire transfers must ensure that all originator information accompanying a wire transfer is retained with the transfer.

rules.title: Beneficiary bank responsibilities
rules.description: A beneficiary bank should have effective risk-based procedures in place to identify wire transfers lacking complete originator information and consider restricting or terminating business relationship with the ordering bank if necessary.
rules.source_clause: A beneficiary bank should have effective risk-based procedures in place to identify wire transfers lacking complete originator information. The lack of complete originator information may be considered as a factor in assessing whether a wire transfer or related transactions are suspicious and whether they should be reported to the Financial Intelligence Unit-India.

rules.title: Appointment of Principal Officer
rules.description: Banks should appoint a senior management officer to be designated as Principal Officer, responsible for monitoring and reporting of all transactions and sharing of information.
rules.source_clause: Banks should appoint a senior management officer to be designated as Principal Officer. Principal Officer shall be located at the head/corporate office of the bank and shall be responsible for monitoring and reporting of all transactions and sharing of information as required under the law.

rules.title: Designated Director
rules.description: Banks are advised to nominate a Director on their Boards as 'Designated Director' to ensure compliance with the obligations under the Prevention of Money Laundering (Amendment) Act, 2012.
rules.source_clause: In view of the above amendment, banks are advised to nominate a Director on their Boards as "Designated Director" to ensure compliance with the obligations under the Prevention of Money Laundering (Amendment) Act, 2012.

rules.title: Maintenance of records of transactions
rules.description: Banks should introduce a system of maintaining proper record of transactions prescribed under Rule 3, including cash transactions over Rs. 10 lakh and suspicious transactions.
rules.source_clause: Banks should introduce a system of maintaining proper record of transactions prescribed under Rule 3, as mentioned below:

rules.title: Information to be maintained
rules.description: Banks are required to maintain the following information, including necessary information required for reconstruction of the transactions: nature of transactions, amount, date, and parties to the transaction.
rules.source_clause: Banks are required to maintain the following information, including necessary information required for reconstruction of the transactions referred to in Rule 3: (a) the nature of the transactions; (b) the amount of the transaction and the currency in which it was denominated; (c) the date on which the transaction was conducted; and (d) the parties to the transaction

rules.title: Maintenance and preservation of records
rules.description: Banks are required to maintain records (hard and soft copies) containing information in respect of transactions for at least ten years from the date of transaction.
rules.source_clause: Banks are required to maintain the records (hard and soft copies) containing information in respect of transactions referred to in Rule 3 above. Banks should take appropriate steps to evolve a system for proper maintenance and preservation of account information in a manner that allows data to be retrieved easily and quickly whenever required or when requested by the competent authorities. Further, banks should maintain for at least ten years from the date of transaction between the bank and the client, all necessary records of transactions, both domestic or international

rules.title: Record Keeping for Customer Identification
rules.description: Banks should ensure that records pertaining to the identification of the customer and his address are properly preserved for at least ten years after the business relationship is ended.
rules.source_clause: Banks should ensure that records pertaining to the identification of the customer and his address (e.g. copies of documents like passports, identity cards, driving licenses, PAN card, utility bills etc.) obtained while opening the account and during the course of business relationship, are properly preserved for at least ten years after the business relationship is ended.

rules.title: Reporting to Financial Intelligence Unit - India
rules.description: Banks are required to report information relating to cash and suspicious transactions to the Director, Financial Intelligence Unit-India (FIU-IND).
rules.source_clause: Banks are required to report information relating to cash and suspicious transactions to the Director, Financial Intelligence Unit-India (FIU-IND) in respect of transactions referred to in Rule 3

rules.title: Suspicious Transaction Reporting
rules.description: Banks should report all suspicious transactions to FIU-IND, even if not completed by customers, irrespective of the amount of the transaction.
rules.source_clause: banks should report all such attempted transactions in STRs, even if not completed by customers, irrespective of the amount of the transaction.

rules.title: Customer Due Diligence
rules.description: Banks should prepare a profile for each customer based on risk categorisation and review it periodically.
rules.source_clause: In terms of instructions contained in paragraph 2.3(b) of this Master Circular, banks are required to prepare a profile for each customer based on risk categorisation.

rules.title: Non-Profit Organization Transaction Reports
rules.description: Banks should maintain proper record of all transactions involving receipts by non-profit organizations of value more than rupees ten lakh or its equivalent in foreign currency and forward a report to FIU-IND.
rules.source_clause: Banks should maintain proper record of all transactions involving receipts by non-profit organizations of value more than rupees ten lakh or its equivalent in foreign currency and to forward a report to FIU-IND of all such transactions in the prescribed format by the 15th of the succeeding month.

rules.title: KYC Documentation
rules.description: Banks should obtain and preserve KYC documents for customers, including proof of identity, address, and other relevant information.
rules.source_clause: Accounts of partnership firms - Legal name, Address, Names of all partners and their addresses, Telephone numbers of the firm and partners

rules.title: Communication of UAPA Nodal Officer Details
rules.description: The IS-I Division in MHA would maintain the consolidated list of all UAPA nodal officers and forward the list to all other UAPA nodal officers.
rules.source_clause: The IS-I Division in MHA would maintain the consolidated list of all UAPA nodal officers and forward the list to all other UAPA nodal officers.

rules.title: Designated List Update and Dissemination
rules.description: The Ministry of External Affairs shall update the list of individuals and entities subject to UN sanction measures on a regular basis and forward the list to the Nodal Officers in Regulators, FIU-IND, IS-I Division, and Foreigners' Division in MHA.
rules.source_clause: 3. (i) The Ministry of External Affairs shall update the list of individuals and entities subject to UN sanction measures on a regular basis. On any revision, the Ministry of External Affairs would electronically forward this list to the Nodal Officers in Regulators, FIU-IND, IS-I Division and Foreigners' Division in MHA.

rules.title: Verification and Freezing of Assets
rules.description: The banks, stock exchanges/depositories, intermediaries regulated by SEBI, and insurance companies shall verify whether individuals or entities listed in the schedule to the Order are holding any funds, financial assets, or economic resources with them and freeze assets if necessary.
rules.source_clause: Maintain updated designated lists in electronic form and run a check on the given parameters on a regular basis to verify whether individuals or entities listed in the schedule to the Order (referred to as designated individuals/entities) are holding any funds, financial assets or economic resources or related services held in the form of bank accounts, stocks or insurance policies etc. with them.

rules.title: Verification of Immovable Properties
rules.description: The UAPA nodal officer of the State/UT shall cause the names of the designated individuals/entities to be verified from the records of the office of the Registrar performing the work of registration of immovable properties in their respective jurisdiction.
rules.source_clause: 7. IS-I Division of MHA would electronically forward the designated lists to the UAPA nodal officer of all States and UTs with the request to have the names of the designated individuals/entities, on the given parameters, verified from the records of the office of the Registrar performing the work of registration of immovable properties in their respective jurisdiction.

rules.title: Timeline for Verification and Action
rules.description: The verification of assets and action to freeze assets shall be completed within a maximum of 5 working days.
rules.source_clause: This verification would be completed within a period not exceeding 5 working days from the date of receipt of such particulars.

rules.title: Freezing of funds and assets of terrorist individuals and entities
rules.description: The UAPA nodal officer of the State/UT shall prevent any individual or entity from making funds, financial assets or economic resources or related services available for the benefit of individuals or entities listed in the schedule to the order or any other person engaged in or suspected to be engaged in terrorism.
rules.source_clause: individual or entity from making any funds, financial assets or economic resources or related services available for the benefit of the individuals or entities listed in the schedule to the order or any other person engaged in or suspected to be engaged in terrorism.

rules.title: Examination of requests for freezing of funds and assets
rules.description: The UAPA nodal officer of IS-I Division of MHA shall examine the request within 5 working days to satisfy itself that the requested designation is supported by reasonable grounds.
rules.source_clause: The UAPA nodal officer of IS-I Division of MHA, shall cause the request to be examined, within 5 working days so as to satisfy itself that on the basis of applicable legal principles, the requested designation is supported by reasonable grounds,

rules.title: Procedure for unfreezing of funds and assets
rules.description: Any individual or entity that has evidence to prove that the freezing of funds, financial assets or economic resources or related services has been inadvertently frozen may move an application to the concerned bank or nodal officer.
rules.source_clause: Any individual or entity, if it has evidence to prove that the freezing of funds, financial assets or economic resources or related services, owned/held by them has been inadvertently frozen, they shall move an application giving the requisite evidence, in writing, to the concerned bank, stock exchanges / depositories, intermediaries regulated by SEBI, insurance companies, Registrar of Immovable Properties and the State/UT nodal officers.

rules.title: Communication of orders under Section 51A of Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act
rules.description: All orders under Section 51A of Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act relating to funds, financial assets or economic resources or related services shall be communicated to all banks, depositories/stock exchanges, intermediaries regulated by SEBI, insurance companies through respective Regulators.
rules.source_clause: All Orders under section 51A of Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, relating to funds, financial assets or economic resources or related services, would be communicated to all banks, depositories/stock exchanges, intermediaries regulated by SEBI, insurance companies through respective Regulators, and to all the Registrars performing the work of registering immovable properties, through the State/UT nodal officer by IS-I Division of MHA.

rules.title: Prevention of entry into or transit through India
rules.description: The Foreigners Division of MHA shall forward the designated lists to the immigration authorities and security agencies with a request to prevent the entry into or the transit through India.
rules.source_clause: As regards prevention of entry into or transit through India of the designated individuals, the Foreigners Division of MHA, shall forward the designated lists to the immigration authorities and security agencies with a request to prevent the entry into or the transit through India.

rules.title: Procedure for communication of compliance of action taken
rules.description: The nodal officers of IS-I Division and Foreigners Division of MHA shall furnish the details of funds, financial assets or economic resources or related services of designated individuals/entities frozen by an order.
rules.source_clause: The nodal officers of IS-I Division and Foreigners Division of MHA shall furnish the details of funds, financial assets or economic resources or related services of designated individuals/entities frozen by an order, and details of the individuals whose entry into India or transit through India was prevented, respectively, to the Ministry of External Affairs for onward communication to the United Nations.

rules.title: e-KYC Service Agreement
rules.description: Any bank willing to use the UIDAI e-KYC service is required to sign an agreement with the UIDAI.
rules.source_clause: Any bank willing to use the UIDAI e-KYC service is required to sign an agreement with the UIDAI.

rules.title: Biometric Scanner Certification
rules.description: Banks must deploy STQC Institute, Department of Electronics & Information Technology, Government of India certified biometric scanners at bank branches/micro ATMs/BC points as per UIDAI standards.
rules.source_clause: These should be Standardisation Testing and Quality Certification (STQC) Institute, Department of Electronics & Information Technology, Government of India certified biometric scanners at bank branches/ micro ATMs/ BC points as per UIDAI standards.

rules.title: Software Application Development
rules.description: Banks must develop a software application to enable use of e-KYC across various Customer Service Points (CSP) as per UIDAI defined Application Programming Interface (API) protocols.
rules.source_clause: Develop a software application to enable use of e-KYC across various Customer Service Points (CSP) (including bank branch, BCs etc.) as per UIDAI defined Application Programming Interface (API) protocols.

rules.title: Customer Authorization
rules.description: Banks must define a procedure for obtaining customer authorization to UIDAI for sharing e-KYC data with the bank.
rules.source_clause: Define a procedure for obtaining customer authorization to UIDAI for sharing e-KYC data with the bank.

rules.title: KYC Norms and AML Standards
rules.description: Banks must comply with Know Your Customer (KYC) Norms and Anti-Money Laundering (AML) Standards.
rules.source_clause: Prevention of Money Laundering

rules.title: Prevention of Money Laundering Act
rules.description: Banks must comply with the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002.
rules.source_clause: Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002 – Obligation of banks in terms of Rules notified thereunder.

rules.title: Acceptance of Aadhaar Letter
rules.description: Aadhaar letter can be accepted as a proof of both identity and address if the address provided by the account holder is the same as that on Aadhaar letter.
rules.source_clause: If the address provided by the account holder is the same as that on Aadhaar letter, it may be accepted as a proof of both identity and address.

rules.title: Introduction Not Mandatory
rules.description: Introduction from an existing customer is not mandatory for opening bank accounts.
rules.source_clause: Since introduction is not mandatory for opening of accounts under PML Act and Rules or Reserve Bank’s extant KYC instructions, banks should not insist on introduction for opening bank accounts of customers.

rules.title: Small Account Definitions
rules.description: In terms of Rule 2 clause (fb) of the Notification 'small account' means a savings account in a banking company where- (i) the aggregate of all credits in a financial year does not exceed Rupees one lakh; (ii) the aggregate of all withdrawals and transfers in a month does not exceed Rupees ten thousand; and (iii) the balance at any point of time does not exceed Rupees fifty thousand.
rules.source_clause: In terms of Rule 2 clause (fb) of the Notification 'small account' means a savings account in a banking company where- (i) the aggregate of all credits in a financial year does not exceed Rupees one lakh; (ii) the aggregate of all withdrawals and transfers in a month does not exceed Rupees ten thousand; and (iii) the balance at any point of time does not exceed Rupees fifty thousand.

rules.title: Record-Keeping for 'At Par' Cheques
rules.description: Banks should maintain records pertaining to issuance of 'at par' cheques covering inter alia the applicant's name and account number, beneficiary's details, and date of issuance of the 'at par' cheque.
rules.source_clause: (i) records pertaining to issuance of 'at par' cheques covering inter alia the applicant's name and account number, beneficiary's details and date of issuance of the 'at par' cheque,

rules.title: Employee Training
rules.description: Banks must have an ongoing employee training programme so that the members of the staff are adequately trained in KYC procedures.
rules.source_clause: Banks must have an ongoing employee training programme so that the members of the staff are adequately trained in KYC procedures.

rules.title: Opening of small account
rules.description: An individual who desires to open a small account in a banking company may be allowed to open such an account on production of a self-attested photograph and affixation of signature or thumb print.
rules.source_clause: Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-rule (2), an individual who desires to open a small account in a banking company may be allowed to open such an account on production of a self-attested photograph and affixation of signature or thumb print, as the case may be, on the form for opening the account.

rules.title: Foreign Contribution Regulation
rules.description: Banks should ensure that the provisions of Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 1976 as amended from time to time, wherever applicable, are strictly adhered to.
rules.source_clause: (iii) Banks should ensure that the provisions of Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 1976 as amended from time to time, wherever applicable, are strictly adhered to.

rules.title: Enhanced Monitoring for PEPs
rules.description: Banks should subject accounts of PEPs to enhanced monitoring on an ongoing basis.
rules.source_clause: The decision to open an account for PEP should be taken at a senior level which should be clearly spelt out in Customer Acceptance Policy. Banks should also subject such accounts to enhanced monitoring on an ongoing basis.

rules.title: Risk-Based Approach for High-Risk Products and Customers
rules.description: Banks are required to adopt enhanced measures for products, services, and customers with a medium or high-risk rating.
rules.source_clause: As a corollary, banks would be required to adopt enhanced measures for products, services and customers with a medium or high risk rating.

rules.title: Reporting of Matches with UNSCR Lists
rules.description: Banks shall immediately, not later than 24 hours from the time of finding out such customer, inform full particulars of the funds, financial assets or economic resources or related services held in the form of bank accounts, held by such customer.
rules.source_clause: (ii) In case, the particulars of any of their customers match with the particulars of designated individuals/entities, the banks shall immediately, not later than 24 hours from the time of finding out such customer, inform full particulars of the funds, financial assets or economic resources or related services held in the form of bank accounts, held by such customer on their books to the Joint Secretary (IS-I), Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) at FAX No. 011-23092569 and also convey over telephone on 011-23092736.

rules.title: Implementation of UN Security Council Resolution 1373
rules.description: Countries are obligated to freeze without delay the funds or other assets of persons who commit, or attempt to commit, terrorist acts or participate in or facilitate the commission of terrorist acts.
rules.source_clause: U.N. Security Council Resolution 1373 obligates countries to freeze without delay the funds or other assets of persons who commit, or attempt to commit, terrorist acts or participate in or facilitate the commission of terrorist acts;

rules.title: Definition of Beneficial Owner
rules.description: The term 'Beneficial Owner' refers to the natural person who ultimately owns or controls a client and/or the person on whose behalf the transaction is being conducted.
rules.source_clause: The term ‘Beneficial Owner’ has been defined as the natural person who ultimately owns or controls a client and / or the person on whose behalf the transaction is being conducted, and includes a person who exercises ultimate effective control over a juridical person.

rules.title: Non-Face-to-Face Customer Verification
rules.description: Banks should have specific and adequate procedures to mitigate the higher risk involved in non-face-to-face customer verification.
rules.source_clause: In the case of non-face-to-face customers, apart from applying the usual Customer Identification Procedure, there must be specific and adequate procedures to mitigate the higher risk involved.

rules.title: Verification of Proprietary Concern Documents
rules.description: Banks should call for and verify specific documents before opening accounts in the name of a proprietary concern.
rules.source_clause: Apart from following the extant guidelines on Customer Identification Procedure as applicable to the proprietor, banks should call for and verify the following documents before opening of accounts in the name of a proprietary concern:

rules.title: Salaried Employee Account Verification
rules.description: Banks should not rely solely on a certificate/letter issued by the employer for KYC purposes; instead, they should insist on at least one officially valid document.
rules.source_clause: It has been brought to our notice that for opening bank accounts of salaried employees some banks rely on a certificate / letter issued by the employer as the only KYC document for the purposes of certification of identity as well as address proof.

rules.title: Foreign Student Account Requirements
rules.description: Banks may open a Non Resident Ordinary (NRO) bank account of a foreign student on the basis of their passport and a letter offering admission from the educational institution.
rules.source_clause: RRBs and StCBs/CCBs authorized to open / maintain NRE / NRO accounts may open a Non Resident Ordinary (NRO) bank account of a foreign student on the basis of his / her passport (with appropriate visa and immigration endorsement) which contains the proof of identity and address in the home country along with a photograph and a letter offering admission from the educational institution.

rules.title: Self Help Group (SHG) Account Requirements
rules.description: KYC verification of all the members of SHG need not be done while opening the savings bank account of the SHG; KYC verification of all the office bearers would suffice.
rules.source_clause: In order to address the difficulties faced by Self Help Groups (SHGs) in complying with KYC norms while opening savings bank accounts and credit linking of their accounts, it is clarified that KYC verification of all the members of SHG need not be done while opening the savings bank account of the SHG and KYC verification of all the office bearers would suffice.
